title: Lesson 10 - Prompt Template Lifecycle: Activation, Versions, and Invocation
description: Explain the process for creating, activating, and executing prompt templates.

questions.question: A consultant activates version 1 of a template, then needs to change its wording. What must they do?
options: Edit version 1 directly, because it is the active version
Save as a New Version and edit that, because version 1 is now immutable
Deactivate the template, edit version 1, then reactivate it
Delete version 1 and create a new template
questions.explanation: Activation makes a version immutable and even a deactivated but formerly active version stays immutable, so the only way to change the prompt is to save a new version and edit that.

questions.question: What does activating a prompt template version actually do?
options: It makes that version the one available to consuming surfaces, and only one version can be active at a time
It sends the prompt to the model once to warm it up
It copies the template into every agent that references it
It converts the template into an Apex class
questions.explanation: Activation selects which single version is available to the surfaces that call the template, so it is a control over availability and not a change to the template content.

questions.question: An agent is running an active template and someone edits the prompt. What do users see?
options: The edited prompt on the next turn, because editing is immediate
An error until the template is reactivated
A blend of the old and new prompt
The currently active version unchanged, until a new version is activated
questions.explanation: Running surfaces resolve against the active version, so a draft edit is invisible to them and the switch happens only when a different version is activated.
